sources.title: ‘Sense and Sensibility’ Costume Designer on Blending Historical Accuracy and Modern Styling for the Dashwood Sisters: ‘We Want to Do Jane Austen Justice’

discussion.body: Chaptering a wardrobe by country and city is a tidy way to make a two-hour adaptation legible — the audience learns the emotional map of the film partly through hemlines and bonnets.
Or it risks making place do work that character should. Two sisters who are supposed to differ in temperament shouldn't be distinguishable mainly by postcode.

items.title: Sense and Sensibility, Dressed in Two Chapters: Country and City
items.body: Georgia Oakley's new take on Jane Austen's 1811 novel stars Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles as Elinor and Marianne Dashwood. According to Variety, costume designer Grace Snell approached the job the way a novelist works: in chapters, with the country and the city as the most distinct ones. The first is Barton Cottage, shaped by Devonshire, and it comes before the sisters' world shifts to town. Wardrobe in a period adaptation is also geography — the same family dressed for two different settings, with the move between them doing part of the storytelling work.

sources.title: Do Alberta’s temporary residents pay little tax, reap lots of benefits? We asked economists

discussion.body: The claim treats the province like a till: money in, services out.
Even as a metaphor it says what the vote is about — whether people think the balance is fair, not whether the arithmetic is exact.
Then the number that persuades matters more than the number that balances, and both sides get to choose their own columns.

items.title: Alberta's Referendum Math and the Claim About Temporary Residents' Taxes
items.body: Ahead of an Oct. 19 referendum, Alberta's government has been putting out large dollar figures, and CBC reports that many of them support the claim that temporary residents pay little in taxes compared with what they receive from provincially funded public and social services. That framing is built for a vote: pay in, take out, compare the columns. Which taxes and which services get counted, and over what period, is what decides whether the sentence reads as a scandal or a shrug — and a referendum is precisely a mechanism for finding out which one voters hear.

sources.title: France: Protesters clash with police in nationwide protests, amid rising social polarization

items.title: Hundreds Arrested in France as Price Protests Draw Students, Unions and Yellow Vests
items.body: Students, trade unionists and Yellow Vest activists took to the streets across France to protest high prices and inequality, and police arrested hundreds amid chaotic scenes in cities around the country, Deutsche Welle reports. The composition of the crowds is itself the signal: three constituencies with different grievances — tuition and jobs, contracts and wages, fuel and food — arriving at a shared complaint about the cost of living. Arrest counts measure the temperature of a day like this, not where it ends.

sources.title: House Speaker Mike Johnson draws on faith as he fights to hold the Republican majority

items.title: Johnson Predicts Republicans Keep the House, as PBS Sees Democratic Momentum
items.body: Speaker Mike Johnson says he believes Republicans will hold on to their U.S. House majority, PBS NewsHour reports, pushing back against what the network describes as a surge of Democratic momentum in the final stretch of midterm elections that will determine control of Congress. The 'ever the optimist' label is the network's framing, not his. A speaker predicting his own survival is a cheap bet either way: call it right and you look prescient, call it wrong and no vote has been changed by a forecast.

sources.title: America's politically divided Jewish community braces for Israel's elections

discussion.body: The two positions are answers to different questions: does Netanyahu protect a country central to Jewish identity, or has he damaged its standing abroad? Both framings put Israel first, which is what makes the split feel so personal.
Or they are answers to the same question — does this government help or hurt Israel? — which makes it less a clash of priorities than a straight disagreement about consequences.

items.title: Two Views of Netanyahu Among Jewish Americans
items.body: PBS NewsHour reports a politically divided Jewish American community when it comes to Benjamin Netanyahu. His supporters, especially among Orthodox Jews, believe he is protecting a country they love and see as central to their identity. Many liberal and younger Jewish Americans read the same government the other way, saying his policies have harmed Israel's standing in the world. The two camps are not arguing about whether Israel matters. They are arguing about whether this prime minister helps or hurts the thing they both care about, which is why the disagreement has such a sharp edge to it.

sources.title: Family of Quebec boy killed while cycling calls off ghost bike memorial, cites hate messages

items.title: A Quebec Family Called Off a Ghost Bike Memorial After Hate Messages
items.body: An 11-year-old boy was fatally struck while riding his bicycle in Quebec City's Beauport borough. CBC reports that his family had planned to install a ghost bike in his honour this weekend, and has now called the memorial off, citing hateful messages they received. A roadside tribute meant to mark a child's death became one more thing the family had to absorb.

sources.title: Gene Schwam, Veteran Hollywood Publicist to Elvis Presley, Julie Andrews and More, Dies at 96

items.title: The Publicist Whose Client List Ran From Elvis to Lenny Bruce
items.body: Gene Schwam, a veteran Hollywood publicist who represented top talent including Elvis Presley, Blake Edwards, Julie Andrews, Barbara Eden and Lenny Bruce, died Friday in Los Angeles after a brief illness. He was 96. In 1955 he co-founded Hanson & Schwam Public Relations with Adeline Hanson, an independent publicity agency that would last for decades. That roster is a small portrait of what mid-century American entertainment contained: a rock-and-roll icon, a musical-comedy star and a comedian who made his name on the club circuit, all handled by the same shop.

sources.title: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery

items.title: Pope Leo XIV Leaves a Rome Hospital After Lung Cancer Surgery
items.body: NPR reports that Pope Leo XIV left Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Saturday, days after surgery for lung cancer removed the lower lobe of his right lung. The next fixed item on the calendar, as the network describes it, is a trip to Latin America in November, currently scheduled.

sources.title: Quebec author abandons effort to document novel’s origins amid AI allegations

discussion.body: Abandoning the documentation isn't proof of anything. It just means the claim he disputes stays on the record unanswered, and readers will draw their own conclusion from the silence.

Fair — but the asymmetry is the story worth noticing. The accusation needs no file, while the defence requires one, and the burden lands on whoever was accused. That is a strange new clause in the contract between a writer and a reader.

items.title: A Quebec Author Stops Trying to Document How He Wrote His Novel
items.body: Thélyson Orélien, a Quebec author, has abandoned efforts to compile evidence supporting his denial that artificial intelligence was used to write his novel, his publisher confirmed to Global News. The allegation, in other words, arrives complete; the rebuttal has to be assembled after the fact, out of a paper trail a novelist never expected to need. Whether that trail could have settled anything is the part nobody gets to find out now.

sources.title: John Wilson’s Next Documentary Will Reportedly Show Audiences ‘How to’ Tour Like Harry Styles

items.title: John Wilson's Next Documentary Turns to Harry Styles' Tour
items.body: IndieWire reports that John Wilson, coming off his feature debut “The History of Concrete,” has turned his camera onto Harry Styles and his recent tour. That is the pitch in full: a documentarian the outlet calls beloved, pointed at a stadium pop machine. Whether the result is about the music, the crowd or the logistics of the thing, the juxtaposition is doing most of the work before a frame is shown.

sources.title: Dozens of critically endangered orangutans rescued from Indonesian wildfires

items.title: Dozens of Critically Endangered Orangutans Rescued From Indonesian Wildfires
items.body: NPR reports that rescuers in Indonesia have saved dozens of orangutans from wildfires. The species is critically endangered, and the fires it is facing this season threaten both the animals and their habitat, not just their immediate escape routes. Dozens is a real number for a species this depleted, and a small one against a deadly burning season — a rescue holding a line rather than a recovery.

sources.title: Stellantis workers begin voting on strike mandate as talks remain stalled

items.title: Stellantis Workers in Canada Vote on a Strike Mandate as Talks Stall
items.body: Stellantis workers in Canada have begun voting on whether to give their union a strike mandate, with collective bargaining negotiations stalled, Global News Canada reports. The vote is authorization rather than a walkout: it decides whether the union holds the option of calling one. Everything after that depends on bargaining that, by this account, has not moved.

sources.title: Fuel costs squeezing margins for some businesses

items.title: Diesel Above £2 a Litre, and a Duty Freeze That May Not Be Enough
items.body: BBC Business reports that diesel recently topped £2 per litre, and that there is concern a duty freeze will not go far enough. The pressure lands on businesses that buy fuel as an input: fuel costs are squeezing margins for some of them, which means the increase is being absorbed rather than passed along in full. A frozen duty holds one component of the pump price still; it does nothing about the rest of the rise.

sources.title: Femicide in Iran: When 'honor' becomes a death sentence

items.title: Iran's Debate Over So-Called 'Honour' Killings Restarts With Another Killing
items.body: DW reports that the murder of a young mother has once again sparked debate in Iran over so-called honour killings, along with the social acceptance of violence against women and the lack of protection for people vulnerable to gender-based violence. The 'once again' is the substance: a killing that reopens an argument about how much violence against women is tolerated, and about who is left exposed to it. Naming social acceptance and missing protection pushes the question past any single perpetrator.

sources.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies

discussion.body: The direction of travel is the interesting part: restrictions written by Congress, suspended by the president, with national security given as the reason.
But 'temporarily' is doing real work there. A pause that can be reversed is a different instrument from a repeal, and it says something about how the move is meant to be read.

items.title: The US President Temporarily Suspends Sanctions That Congress Just Passed
items.body: The US president has temporarily ended many of the restrictions on Moscow that Congress recently passed, citing national security concerns, the BBC reports. Two words carry the weight here. 'Temporarily' means this is a pause rather than a repeal, an instrument that can be reversed — and reversibility is itself a form of leverage. The other word is Congress: the measures being switched off originated in the legislature, not the White House, which puts the executive branch in the position of suspending penalties another branch wrote into law. The stated justification is national security; the structural oddity is the part worth watching.

sources.title: Michael Forest Dies: Actor In Roger Corman B-Movies, ‘Star Trek’s Apollo Was 97

items.title: A Character Actor's Range: Corman B-Movies, Anime Voices, and Scores of TV Guest Spots
items.body: Deadline reports the death of Michael Forest, a prolific and longtime character actor. His credits sketch a whole mode of working life in American screen acting: the B movies of Roger Corman, voice work on numerous anime projects, and guest appearances in scores of television series — The Adventures of Rin Tin Tin, The Twilight Zone, The Dick Van Dyke Show, Silk Stalkings and daytime soaps among them. That is the résumé of someone hired to be vivid for a scene and then disappear. The through-line isn't a genre, it's the willingness to turn up in all of them.

sources.title: Teaching students to think and learn through questions

items.title: OpenAI's Educator Tools Arrive in Brazilian Portuguese
items.body: OpenAI says it is marking Teachers' Day by making AI for Educators available in Brazilian Portuguese, and points teachers toward Study Mode, which the company describes as helping them support active, step-by-step learning. The language expansion is the checkable part: a product now exists in a market where it previously didn't. The pedagogical framing is the company's own description of its own tool, which is a weaker kind of statement than a result. Worth keeping the two apart whenever a classroom product arrives with a theory of learning attached.
